name: Web pages & RSS
description: Articles from an RSS or Atom feed, and the content and links of any web page.

objects.label: articles
objects.description: Entries in an RSS or Atom feed, newest first.

fields.label: summary
fields.description: The short description the feed provides. Some feeds put the whole article here.

fields.label: full text
fields.description: The article body when the feed includes it; otherwise fetched from the link.

fields.label: category
fields.description: A tag or section the feed assigns, such as Security or Product.

objects.label: web pages
objects.description: A page fetched from an address, as readable text. Filter on last changed to watch a page for changes.

fields.label: page text
fields.description: The readable text of the page without navigation, menus and ads.

fields.label: last changed
fields.description: When the page text last differed from the previous fetch.

objects.label: links on a page
objects.description: Every link found on a page. Useful for picking up new PDFs or documents a site posts.

fields.label: type
fields.description: Worked out from the address or file extension.

guidance: Feeds are fetched over plain HTTPS with no login, so nothing is needed beyond outbound web access from wherever the automation runs. Pages are less reliable: layouts change without notice, some sites block automated fetching, and their terms of use or robots.txt may forbid it, so prefer a feed or an API whenever the site offers one. Poll no more often than the content changes; once an hour is plenty for most feeds, and a page behind a login should not be scraped at all.

setup.notes: Nothing to request for public feeds and pages. For content behind a login, ask the site owner for a feed, an API or an export instead of a scraper.
